title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - String Formatting
sourceFile: String Formatting MCQ in C# - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on basics of string formatting in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What are strings in C#?
questions.explanation: Generally, a string is defined as a sequence of characters but it is different in C#. In c++, the string is an array of characters. In case of C#, strings are objects of the built-in string data type. Thus, a string is a reference type.

questions.question: Select the namespace in which string class is built?
questions.explanation: System.String lives in the System namespace. System.Text contains types such as StringBuilder and Encoding, not String.

questions.question: Select the interfaces defined by the string class?
Choose the constructor type used to build strings from character array.

options.text: public String(char[ ] value, int startIndex, int length)

questions.explanation:
public String(char[ ] value) - This form of constructor constructs a string that contains characters in value

public String(char[ ] value, int startIndex, int length) -The second form uses length characters from value, beginning at the index specified by startIndex.

questions.question: Select the operators used for checking the equality in strings:
What does the following C# code set specifies?
questions.code: public static int Compare(string strA, string strB)

options.text: Comparison is case and culture sensitive
Two strings A and B are compared with each other
Output is : >0 for (A > B), <0 for (A < B) else '0' for(A=B)

questions.explanation: Compares the string referred to by strA with strB. Returns greater than zero if strA is greater than strB, less than zero if strA is less than strB, and zero if strA and strB are equal. The comparison is case and culture-sensitive.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation:
'+' concatenates with no extra spaces, so "Hello" + "c" + "Sharp" is HellocSharp.

Output :

HellocSharp

questions.question: Which of these operators can be used to concatenate two or more String objects?
What does the following C# code set specify?
questions.code: public static int Compare(string strA, int indexA, string strB, int indexB, int length, bool ignoreCase)

options.text: Comparison begins at strA[indexA] and strB[indexB] and runs for length of characters
Returns output > 0 for for strA > strB else < 0 for strA < strB else if strA = str B output is 0
Comparison is culture sensitive and if ignore case is true, comparison ignores case differences

questions.explanation: Compares portions of the strings referred to by strA and strB. The comparison begins at strA[indexA] and strB[indexB] and runs for length characters. Returns greater than zero if strA is greater than strB, less than zero if strA is less than strB, and zero if strA and strB are equal. If ignoreCase is true, the comparison ignores case differences. Otherwise, case differences matter. The comparison is culture-sensitive.

questions.question: Which string operation does the below-mentioned method define?
questions.code: public static string Concat(string str0, string str1)

options.text: string str1 is concatenated to the end of str0
can be used to concatenate any number of strings

questions.explanation:
This method returns a string that contains str1 concatenated to the end of str0. Another form of Concat(), shown here, concatenates three strings:

public static string Concat(string str0, string str1, string str2). Hence, any number of strings can be concatenated using this method.

questions.question: Choose the base class for string() method.
questions.explanation: String is an alias for the predefined "System.string" class from which most of the string() methods are derived.

questions.question: Did method use to remove whitespace from the string?
questions.explanation: Trim() removes leading and trailing whitespace. TrimStart() removes from the start only; TrimEnd() removes from the end only.
